changes.before: Create an ordinary table readings(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,value INTEGER). Insert ID1 text 17 and ID2 text unknown. Create observed(id,kind) exposing typeof(value). This task deliberately observes flexible affinity rather than rejecting text.
changes.after: Check the kind of value SQLite actually stored.

before: Ordinary SQLite tables use flexible value types. A column declared INTEGER has integer affinity: it tries suitable numeric conversion when storing a value, but its declaration alone does not reject every nonnumeric text. This differs from rigid typing in many other database systems.

typeof(value) returns the stored value's storage-class name, such as integer, real, text, blob or null. It inspects a value, not the column declaration. In an INTEGER-affinity column, '12' can be stored as integer 12, while 'twelve' remains text. Use STRICT or appropriate constraints when that flexibility is not your intended contract.

Application: Create an ordinary table readings(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,value INTEGER). Insert ID1 text 17 and ID2 text unknown. Create observed(id,kind) exposing typeof(value). This task deliberately observes flexible affinity rather than rejecting text.
after: An ordinary SQLite column has a preferred type, called its affinity. An INTEGER column tries to store suitable values as whole numbers. That declaration alone does not refuse every other kind of value.
`typeof(value)` reports the kind of value actually stored, such as `integer`, `real`, `text`, or `null`. It does not just repeat the column's declared type.

The numeric text can be converted; the word cannot. Ordinary SQLite tables allow this flexibility. Use stricter table rules when accepting text would break your program. The next lesson shows one way.

Create ordinary `readings(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, value INTEGER)`. Insert quoted text `'17'` at id `1` and `'unknown'` at id `2`. Create `observed(id, kind)` using typeof to show how each value was stored.

before.question: An ordinary INTEGER-affinity column receives the text cloudy. What can SQLite store without an additional constraint?
choices: The integer zero in every case
before.explanation: A nonnumeric text that cannot be converted may remain text in an ordinary flexible table.

after.question: An ordinary INTEGER column has no extra rule. What can SQLite store when given the text cloudy?
after.explanation: The word cannot become a number, so it can remain text in an ordinary SQLite table.
